title:
Super Ionic Li
                    <sub>3–2x</sub>
                    M
                    <sub>x</sub>
                    (OH)
                    <sub>1-y</sub>
                    N
                    <sub>y</sub>
                    Cl (M=Ca, W, N=F) Halide Hydroxide as an Anti-Perovskite Electrolyte for Solid-State Batteries
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Lithium halide hydroxide (Li
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    OHX) as a new class of low-cost, lightweight solid electrolyte (SSE) shows promising lithium-ion conductivity for advanced solid-state batteries. Here, using solid-state synthesis and extensive materials characterization, the impurity-free Li
                    <jats:sub>3–2x</jats:sub>
                    M
                    <jats:sub>x</jats:sub>
                    (OH)
                    <jats:sub>1-y</jats:sub>
                    N
                    <jats:sub>y</jats:sub>
                    Cl (M=Ca, W, N=F) are reported, having
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>
                        
                      </jats:tex-math>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msub>
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mi>σ</mml:mi>
                          </mml:mrow>
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mi mathvariant="italic">gb</mml:mi>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:msub>
                        <mml:mo>=</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mn>23.7</mml:mn>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    mS cm
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    and
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>
                        
                      </jats:tex-math>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msub>
                          <mml:mi mathvariant="italic">σ</mml:mi>
                          <mml:msub>
                            <mml:mi>b</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mspace width="0.25em"/>
                          </mml:msub>
                        </mml:msub>
                        <mml:mo>=</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mn>9.6</mml:mn>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    mS cm
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    at 140 °C for
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>
                        
                      </jats:tex-math>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mi>x</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>=</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mi>y</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>=</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mn>0</mml:mn>
                        <mml:mo>.</mml:mo>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    Substituted smaller anionic dopants, such as
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>
                        
                      </jats:tex-math>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:msup>
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mi mathvariant="normal">F</mml:mi>
                          </mml:mrow>
                          <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                        </mml:msup>
                        <mml:mo>,</mml:mo>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    facilitate the movement of Li ions within the anti-perovskite framework through rotational disordering in local coordination, resulting in the highest ion conductivity of 0.28 mS cm
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    at 25 °C. Using a strong combination of XRD, FTIR, pH, elemental EDS analysis, and calculated activation energies, it is demonstrated that the presence of H in these SSEs yields significantly higher Li
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    -ionic conductivity. Rotation of an OH-group in enlarged Cl-O-Cl triangular in the synthesized SSEs and their fully defected/ disordered structures enhance Li-ion conductivity.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:inline-formula/>
                  </jats:p>
